description: Henri II pledges Anzeling (high, middle and low justice) to Henriette de Vaudémont, January 1624.
Hestroff pledged to Henriette de Vaudémont; p. 51 says January 1624, p. 50 January 1625.
February 1620: the Conseil d'État maintains the abbot of Freistroff in the middle and low justice against the ducal procurator's claim of 1616.
Accommodation of 28-30 July 1620 between Lorraine and Trier confirms undivided joint sovereignty and common justice; approved by Ferdinand II on 4 December 1623.
Same accommodation of July 1620 for the Merzig part of the condominium.
Judgment of the Imperial Chamber of Speyer, 7 July 1629: the castle and town of Sarrewerden, as masculine fiefs of Metz, go to François II.
Same Speyer judgment of 7 July 1629 for Bouquenom.
31 July 1629: Lorraine troops take Bouquenom by force and occupy the whole county, beyond what the judgment granted.
François II dies 14 October 1632; Charles IV takes the oath of the county's subjects the next day.
Élisée d'Haraucourt buys the shares of the count of Vaudémont and his wife Christine de Salm in the lordship of Faulquemont.
In December 1629 Charles IV raises the lordship of Faulquemont to a marquisate for the Haraucourt family.
Henri II gives Louis de Guise the lordship of Boulay for life; he then styles himself count of Boulay.
January 1625: Louis de Guise and Henriette do homage to Charles IV and Nicole for Phalsbourg, Hombourg, Saint-Avold and the county of Boulay.
After Louis de Guise's death Henriette receives the county of Boulay in dower from Charles IV, for a loan of 300,000 francs (reversal letters 1 April 1633).
By his will of November 1621 Henri II leaves Henriette 300,000 francs, secured by a pledge of the county of Bitche.
Téterchen is pledged to Louis de Guise as security for a loan of 100,000 francs, formerly secured on Preny.
Goods at Roupeldange, with Téterchen, are pledged to Louis de Guise as security for a loan of 100,000 francs.
notes: goods only; dated by the surrounding text

description: Henri II sells the lordship of Hestroff and Anzeling to André des Bordes, governor of Sierck, for 10,000 francs.
Henri II sells the lordship of Hestroff and Anzeling to André des Bordes, governor of Sierck, for 10,000 francs.
The barony of Dalem, a fief of Lorraine held by Élisée d'Haraucourt, is made a county.
The county of Dalem becomes part of the marquisate of Faulquemont created by Charles IV in December 1629.
Nicolas de Pullenoy does homage for the lordship of Nébing-lès-Albestroff.
Élisée d'Haraucourt founds the new village of Redlach, with the consent of the count of Vaudémont.
Louis de Guise founds the village of Montdidier (1628-29).
Louis de Guise founds the village of Saint-Louis (1628-29).
Louis de Guise founds the village of Bickenholz (1628-29).
February 1629: Emperor Ferdinand II makes Louis de Guise an immediate prince of the Empire for Phalsbourg and Lixheim.
February 1629: Emperor Ferdinand II makes Louis de Guise an immediate prince of the Empire for Phalsbourg and Lixheim.

21 November 1598: once the pledgee Charles of Hohenzollern had renounced, Charles III gives the office of Lemberg back to the count of Hanau, keeping Simten, Vinningen, Riedelberg, Erlenbrunn, Staustein, Imsbach and Ranschborn; Lorraine may reoccupy it if no settlement follows.
Charles III redeems the pledge of his half of Lemberg, giving the castellany of Sarreguemines as security; completed after the count's death in April 1606.

Treaty of February and April 1606 with Hanau-Lichtenberg (ratified in December): Charles III renounces the sovereignty and the office of Lemberg-lès-Pirmasens and cedes Vinningen, Simten and other villages; Hanau gives up its claims on Bitche.
April 1607: Charles III orders the governor of Bitche to evacuate the lordship of Lemberg; Lorraine's half leaves the county of Bitche.
After the death of the count of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen in April 1606, the redemption of Lemberg and Bitche is completed and the settlement ratified in December.
